name: PowerView User Hunting (Find-DomainUserLocation)
description: Find where privileged domain users are currently logged in. CheckAccess verifies if current user has local admin access to those machines.

examples.label: Find DA sessions with local admin check
Stealth mode (DCs and file servers only)

recommended.note: PS Remoting to machine where DA is logged in
Dump DA credentials from that machine
Use DA hash for lateral movement

notes: Queries all machines - very noisy. Use -Stealth to reduce noise. Requires admin rights on targets for -CheckAccess to work.

defense.why_it_works: Find-DomainUserLocation uses NetSessionEnum and NetWkstaUserEnum RPC calls to query each host's active sessions, mapping which privileged users are currently logged on where. Exposes DA session locations - enabling targeted Pass-the-Hash or token impersonation on those hosts.
defense.prerequisites: Any domain user (NetSessionEnum accessible to all by default). PowerView. A host list (from Get-DomainComputer). SMB access (port 445) to target hosts.
defense.impact: T1033 System Owner/User Discovery + T1087.002 Account Discovery. Identifies which host a Domain Admin is currently logged on to - turns credential theft from guesswork to a targeted operation.
defense.detection:
Rapid NetSessionEnum RPC calls (MSRPC \PIPE\srvsvc) to many hosts. Sysmon Event 3: rapid 445 connections to many hosts. Event 4104 SBL: Invoke-UserHunter / Find-DomainUserLocation. MDI: 'SMB session enumeration reconnaissance'.
Monitor for execution of commands and arguments that may be used to gather system and network information (e.g., whoami, id, who, w, groups) particularly when chained with lateral movement behaviors. On Windows, monitor for process creation events for cmd.exe, PowerShell, and net.exe running user discovery commands. On Linux/macOS, monitor shell history and auditd for id, whoami, w, last commands. Correlate discovery activity with subsequent credential access or lateral movement.
defense.artifacts: Sysmon Event 3: rapid 445 connections to many hosts | Event 4104: Find-DomainUserLocation | MDI: SMB session enum recon alert | Netflow: single source → many hosts TCP 445 in short window
defense.splunk_spl:
index=sysmon EventCode=3 DestinationPort=445
| stats dc(DestinationIp) as hosts by SourceHostname, User
| where hosts>20

index=wineventlog EventCode=4104 (ScriptBlockText="*Find-DomainUserLocation*" OR ScriptBlockText="*Invoke-UserHunter*")
| table _time, Computer, User, ScriptBlockText
defense.sentinel_kql:
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where RemotePort == 445
| summarize hosts=dcount(RemoteIP) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 5m)
| where hosts > 20
| sort by hosts desc
defense.prevention:
Restrict NetSessionEnum to admins only (RestrictRemoteSam). Domain Admins log on only from PAWs. Protected Users group for DA accounts. MDI. Credential Guard prevents credential theft even after session enumeration.
This type of attack technique cannot be easily mitigated with preventive controls since it is based on the abuse of system features.
Operating System Configuration: Prevent administrator account enumeration via UAC (GPO: HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\CredUI\EnumerateAdministrators).
User Account Management: Manage creation, modification, use, and permissions associated with user accounts.
defense.evasion: Use -CheckAccess to only hit hosts the current user can admin (fewer connections). Use targeted host list. Add delays between queries.
defense.misconfiguration: NetSessionEnum accessible to all authenticated users (default). DAs log on to regular workstations for daily tasks. No Credential Guard. No PAW model.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# RestrictRemoteSam not configured (default):
(Get-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa').RestrictRemoteSam
# Returns $null = not restricted = any auth user can enumerate sessions

# DA logged onto workstation WS01:
# NetSessionEnum returns: CORP\DomainAdmin1 → WS01 → target for token theft
defense.secure_config:
# Restrict NetSessionEnum:
Set-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa' -Name RestrictRemoteSam -Value 'O:BAG:BAD:(A;;RC;;;BA)'

# PAW model + Authentication Policy Silos:
New-ADAuthenticationPolicySilo -Name 'DomainAdmin-Silo'
# Restrict DA logon to PAW computers only

# Protected Users group:
Add-ADGroupMember -Identity 'Protected Users' -Members 'DomainAdmin1'
# No NTLM, no delegatable credentials, no cached creds on logon

response_steps: Correlate alert with source host, user account, and timestamp
Review Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, Sysmon, PowerShell Script Block / Module Logs, Windows Security Event Log for surrounding context (5 min before/after)
Verify whether the activity matches known administrative baselines or change windows
If confirmed malicious, isolate the host and escalate to incident response

variations.label: Get-NetLoggedon (logged-on users on a host)
variations.description: Enumerates users currently logged into a remote machine via the NetWkstaUserEnum API. Shows interactive and service logon sessions - useful for finding where admins are logged in for credential theft.

variations.label: Get-NetSession (active sessions on a host)
variations.description: Enumerates active SMB sessions on a remote server via the NetSessionEnum API. Shows which users have network connections to the machine - reveals active file sharing and administrative sessions.

variations.label: Get-NetRDPSession (RDP sessions on a host)
variations.description: Enumerates active RDP sessions on a remote machine. Shows which users have remote desktop connections, including disconnected sessions that may still have cached credentials.

variations.label: Get-RegLoggedOn (logged-on via remote registry)
variations.description: Enumerates logged-on users via the remote registry by reading HKU subkeys. Each loaded registry hive corresponds to a logged-in user - an alternative enumeration method when session APIs are restricted.

variations.label: Find-DomainProcess (hunt a process domain-wide)
variations.description: Enumerates running processes on remote machines to find sessions of target users. An alternative to session enumeration - identifies machines where specific users have active processes.

variations.label: Find-DomainUserEvent (logon events for a user)
variations.description: Find-DomainUserEvent (logon events for a user). See the command syntax for exact parameters and flags.

variations.label: Get-DomainUserEvent (4624 logon events on a host)
variations.description: Uses PowerView to enumerate domain user accounts with specific property filters for targeted reconnaissance.

variations.label: Find-DomainLocalGroupMember (local group members domain-wide)
variations.description: Find-DomainLocalGroupMember (local group members domain-wide). See the command syntax for exact parameters and flags.

variations.label: Who is logged on locally (needs local admin)
variations.description: Enumerates locally logged-on users by reading the remote event log for logon events. Works when other session enumeration methods (NetSession, WMI) are blocked or restricted.

variations.label: Last user logged on to a host
variations.description: Last user logged on to a host. See the command syntax for exact parameters and flags.

variations.label: Find-LocalAdminAccess (machines where current user is admin)
variations.description: Uses PowerView to find machines where the current user has local administrator access. Iterates through domain computers testing admin access - identifies lateral movement targets without needing credentials.

variations.label: Test-AdminAccess (test admin on a specific host)
variations.description: Lists active network connections and listening ports. Identifies internal services, database connections, and potential pivoting targets not visible from external scans.

variations.label: Get-NetLocalGroup (local groups on a machine)
variations.description: Get-NetLocalGroup (local groups on a machine). See the command syntax for exact parameters and flags.

explain:
Locates where privileged users are currently logged on, to plan a lateral hop that steals their session:
  Find-DomainUserLocation   query hosts for sessions of high-value users
  -CheckAccess             also test whether YOU are local admin on each host found
Where a DA is logged in AND you have admin, that box is a credential-theft target. Backing cmdlets (Get-NetSession, Get-NetLoggedon, Find-LocalAdminAccess) enumerate sessions and admin access per host.
